newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary O/N rates rise as bids outnumber offers.
newsitem.headline: Hungary O/N rates rise as bids outnumber offers.

text.p: A rise in Hungary's overnight interest rates took traders by surprise on Wednesday as market funds seemed to dry up.
Rates moved at 21 to 21.75 percent in early trade but then rose to around 23 percent as no offers appeared to match bids.
"There were no lenders," said Gabor Liener of Unicbank. "It could be because banks went short at the beginning of the new reserve period but it's difficult to know exactly."

Erika Kaiser of Budapest Bank suggested money was tied up in repo deals after last week's slump in overnight rates to as low as 20.25 percent prompted lenders to move their funds to the central bank, which currently offers a 21 percent one-week reverse repo rate.
"It was very strange today, I can only think all the money went into repo last week," she said, adding that she expected lower tomorrow/next rates of below 22 percent.
